title: NfrClassifierItems
description: Shape of content.items for L1-requirements-nfr-classifier. Like L1-requirements-elicitor's items (and unlike Phase 0's meta-points pattern), every boundary_condition is carried in FULL, not summarized — a boundary condition is already a short, atomic phrase (an explicit number/rule, or the literal 'TBD — needs stakeholder input'), so there is nothing long to condense and no '_summary' suffix convention is needed here. The artifact (nfr-spec.md) still exists as the full, human-readable per-FR table; items restates the same facts in queryable structured form, one entry per requirement, not a condensation of them. Every FR in requirements.md gets exactly one nfr_classifications entry regardless of how many of the six categories apply to it — only the categories genuinely applicable appear in boundary_conditions (kb-L1-nfr-classification-taxonomy's 'apply what's relevant, not a checklist' rule), so array length varies per FR and is never padded to a fixed six. A boundary_condition's source is mechanically constrained below: any condition that is not the literal TBD phrase MUST cite a real, checkable source (requirements.md § FR-NNN, vision.md § <section>, regulatory-feasibility.md § <constraint>, or kb-L1-enterprise-security § ES<n>); a genuinely open condition MUST use the literal TBD phrase and source '—'. Asserting a plausible number with no matching citation, or citing a source for a condition that is actually still open, are both schema violations, not style preferences — this mirrors nfr-spec.template.md's own zero-tolerance rule.

nfr_classifications.description: One entry per functional requirement in requirements.md, same FR ids and same order — never grouped, never reordered.

boundary_condition.description: The boundary condition, carried in full, verbatim — an explicit number/rule directly stated or implied in requirements.md/vision.md/regulatory-feasibility.md/kb-L1-enterprise-security, OR the literal string 'TBD — needs stakeholder input' (optionally prefixed with what is open, e.g. 'Buyer search/discovery response time — TBD — needs stakeholder input') if genuinely ungrounded. Never a plausible-sounding number with no grounded source.

source.description: 'requirements.md § FR-NNN' (the FR's own statement directly implies this boundary), 'vision.md § <section>' (e.g. a North-Star Metric target), 'regulatory-feasibility.md § <constraint>' (a Phase 0 artifact, cited directly — not a KB), 'kb-L1-enterprise-security § ES<n>' (a group policy already resolves this), or '—' ONLY when boundary_condition is the literal TBD phrase.

id.description: The requirements.md FR id this classification is for — never a new id, this agent classifies, it does not create requirements

title.description: Short label matching requirements.md's own FR title — not prose, kept in full

boundary_conditions.description: Every NFR category genuinely applicable to this FR. May be empty (with reasoning stating 'No NFR categories apply') if genuinely none apply — never padded to a fixed six, never silently omitted.

reasoning.description: Explains why each applicable category was flagged and why any grounded value or TBD was assigned — not a re-derivation of the FR's own statement
